candidate_anomalies.code_citation: function t4_decompose_claim, lines 773-774: claim.status = 'supported'; claim.sealed = True
candidate_anomalies.observed_behavior: T4 fires when claim.scope == {} or claim.status == 'underspecified'. At lines 773-774, the parent claim's status is unconditionally set to 'supported' and sealed=True immediately after sub-claims are created. No LLM call evaluates the parent's epistemic status; the LLM is called only to generate sub-claim content. A claim with scope=={} (the standard trigger, since initial claims are generated with scope={}) is sealed as 'supported' regardless of prior status, confidence, or evidence_refs content.

candidate_anomalies.code_citation: function evaluate_branch_claim, lines 484-486: else: claim.status = 'supported'; claim.confidence = 0.85
candidate_anomalies.observed_behavior: For B-prefixed claims, t3_request_evidence calls evaluate_branch_claim(claim). If _llm_json returns None (LLM API failure, JSON parse failure on both first and retry attempts, or any exception), the else branch unconditionally sets claim.status = 'supported' and claim.confidence = 0.85. Code comment at line 473-474 states: 'Falls back to supported+0.85 so T9 can always fire.' The simulated evidence string is appended before evaluate_branch_claim is called, but LLM evaluation failure produces supported+0.85 regardless of claim content.

candidate_anomalies.code_citation: select_operation lines 1015-1017: all(c.status == 'supported' for c in branches); select_focus_claim lines 1067-1069: all(c.status == 'supported' for c in children)
candidate_anomalies.observed_behavior: Both select_operation and select_focus_claim use c.status == 'supported' as the T9 readiness criterion, not c.sealed == True. Branch claims receive status='supported' from T6 (line 868) or T3's evaluate_branch_claim (line 482 or 485). Neither T6 nor T3 sets sealed=True; that requires a subsequent T8 firing. Therefore T9 can fire while all branches have status='supported' but sealed=False. T8 on the branch claims fires in a subsequent iteration after T9 has already executed.
